# Models and materials {#sec-app-materials}

**Models.** Qwen3 1.7B, 4B, 8B, 14B and 32B (`Qwen/Qwen3-*`), and Qwen3 8B and 14B
base (`Qwen/Qwen3-*-Base`). Gemma 3 1B, 4B, 12B and 27B instruction-tuned
(`google/gemma-3-*-it`), and Gemma 3 12B pretrained (`google/gemma-3-12b-pt`).
Qwen3.5 4B, 9B and 27B (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-*`). Gemma 4 31B (`google/gemma-4-31B-it`) for
the hidden choice [@gemma4]. Qwen3 0.6B, 1.7B and 4B for the a/an analysis, with the
per-layer transcoders of @hanna2026latent. All models run in bfloat16 on
Apple silicon (PyTorch MPS), with full recomputation and no key-value cache across
edited runs.

**Couplet prompts.** The chat format of @hanna2026latent. The user turn is
"Write only the next line of this rhyming couplet: {line 1}", preceded by
`/no_think` for Qwen3. The plain format of @ma2026plan is `A rhyming couplet:\n{line
1}\n`, with no template; line 2 is the continuation up to the next newline. Rhymes use
the perfect-rhyme sets of the Datamuse API, following @hanna2026latent. The outcome
uses the single-token words of each set.

**Item construction.** Qwen3 1.7B to 14B use the released 100-couplet steering
subsets and donor pairings of @hanna2026latent. Other models use their rule: the
first 100 first lines, in their order, that the model rhymes, with donors of a
different rhyme group drawn with seed 20260925. Hidden-choice lists are drawn from 8
single-token fruits (4-item lists) or from the first 12 single-token animals of a
fixed 16-word pool (6-item lists), with seed 20260925. Chains and sums are drawn with
the same seed, balanced over first digits.

**Batching.** Where batched, forward passes group sequences of equal length only; we
found that left padding shifts positions in patched forward passes. Batched and
unbatched cells agree to a median of 0.05 and a maximum of 0.13 log-odds in a
reference check. Batched generation uses left padding with per-row patches. It
reproduces unbatched greedy generations in 7 of 8 checks, and the remaining one is
a bfloat16 near-tie.

# The six-cell assay for single-token mediators {#sec-app-sixcell}

For a mediator token \(B\) with support \(\{b_0,b_1\}\), the six cells are
\(I\in\{0,1\}\times B\in\{\text{free},\operatorname{do}(b_0),\operatorname{do}(b_1)\}\).
Free generation is a policy, not a third value of \(B\). With \(B_i\) the greedy
mediator under \(I=i\) and \(Y(i,b)\) the continuation distribution, the total effect
\(Y(1,B_1)-Y(0,B_0)\) splits exactly into emission \(Y(0,B_1)-Y(0,B_0)\) and
persistence \(Y(1,B_1)-Y(0,B_1)\). Under a stochastic policy \(q_i(b)\), emission is
\(\sum_b [q_1(b)-q_0(b)]\,Y(0,b)\), which gives the leverage identity of @sec-emission
for binary mediators. The multi-token version of @sec-method replaces the mediator
with the generated text \(g\).

# Decision rules committed before the results {#sec-app-prereg}

After the initial couplet split, every experiment's design, decision rule and
predictions were committed to the project repository before its first result. These
are commitments in version control, not entries in an external registry. @tbl-prereg
lists each rule with the commit that recorded it (committer time, UTC+9) and its
outcome. Deviations are dated in each experiment's record. The main ones:

- the text-swap reference in the hidden choice, added after a 3-pair smoke test at
  1.7B and before any real run;
- pick specificity, added post hoc for fruits, then committed as the primary measure
  of the animal replication before its result;
- the absolute-relay reading rule for distance, added after the full-attention
  control and before the Gemma 3 result;
- the fast path for the Qwen3.5-27B pilot (24 couplets, screen generations reused),
  committed before its result;
- the block edit for chains, added after the first 8B rows and before any 14B or 32B
  run;
- for the submission deadline, the 27B window curve shortened to 18 couplets, and the
  checks listed in @sec-limitations not run, recorded before the affected results.

**Anchor specificity** (persistence, donor states at one position of line 1). At
Qwen3-1.7B: the rhyme word \(+12.1\), end of turn \(+6.0\), punctuation \(+5.7\), a
middle word \(+5.5\), the first word \(+3.5\). At 8B: \(+22.6\), \(+10.6\), \(+10.7\), \(+8.6\)
and \(+5.1\). At 32B: \(+22.2\), \(+11.0\), \(+11.5\), \(+4.5\) and \(+3.8\). At Gemma 3 12B:
\(+41.2\), \(+15.3\), \(+14.2\), \(+10.9\) and \(+7.9\). Relay is small from every position.

**Converging evidence from the released attention intervention.** @hanna2026latent
block the heads that read the rhyme word near the end of line 2. Afterwards only 30%,
20%, 13% and 32% of couplets still rhyme at 1.7B, 4B, 8B and 14B, all of which rhymed
before. Direct retrieval is necessary, and relay does not replace it.

:::

At Qwen3-4B, the forced sentence positions hold a small part of the pick,
\(+0.57\) [0.48, 0.67] or about 5% of the text swap. The donor run's sentence positions
read this directly from the list. In Qwen3 at 8B and larger and in Gemma 3 the sentence
positions hold about nothing (Qwen3-32B about 1%); in the Qwen3.5 hybrids they hold 8%
(9B) and 7% (27B, \(+0.15\) [0.12, 0.18]) of the text-swap effect.

# Relationship to an earlier workshop version {#sec-app-workshop}

A non-archival workshop version of this work introduced the emission and persistence
decomposition, there called public and private routes, on Gemma 3 270M and 1B with
sparse-feature and residual interventions on the article *a/an*. That version also
reported *mediator-relative routing*: target-directed interventions appeared to shift
toward the emission route when two alternatives required different articles. A
construction audit, frozen before its result, retracts that claim. The
named-donor direction contains an article-readout component, about 4% of its norm.
Removing it leaves lexical efficacy unchanged but removes nearly all of the route
shift: the paired interaction falls from 0.120 [0.079, 0.161] to 0.018
[\(-0.000\), 0.038]. The component alone reproduces most of the shift. The route shift
was therefore a property of how the intervention vector was built, not of the model.
The present paper keeps the decomposition, extends it to paths within persistence and
to multi-token generation, and replaces the small-model experiments with the study
reported here.

# Compute {#sec-app-compute}

Experiments ran on one Apple M1 laptop (16 GB) and one Apple M4 Max workstation
(128 GB unified memory), with no GPU cluster. Jobs were scheduled under a declared
memory budget and checkpointed per item, so interrupted runs resume without loss. A
27B to 32B couplet chain (screen, edit and generation, route split, position split and
necessity) takes one to three hours. The hidden-choice runs take 10 to 30 minutes
per model.
